```

Do not stream from a mutable Hub name during any probe.

### B. Hash and join receipt

For both artifacts:

- Preserve repository ID, full commit SHA, retrieval time, license hash, file list, file sizes, and every HF metadata revision.
- SHA-256 every regular artifact file, excluding only download-control metadata.
- Produce the scorecard full-tree root digest and the JouleWise weight-only folded identity.
- Require every `.metadata` first line to equal the ratified revision.
- Compare tokenizer files, special-token maps, chat-template bytes, vocabulary size, BOS/EOS sets, and realized prompt-token hashes byte-for-byte.
- Verify both configs are 4-bit, group size 64, same Qwen3 generation/tuning state, and compatible with the ratified output policies.
- Preserve the common `selection_join_key`; a nonjoining receipt fails DG2.

### C. Load and memory probe

The host is an M3 Max with 128 GB unified memory. Apply the already-ratified D-071 shape:

- Batch 1.
- Exact 8,192-token prompt.
- Empty KV cache.
- Exactly 128 EOS-masked greedy decode tokens.
- No offload, swap, prefix cache, or expert streaming.
- Three fresh processes per artifact; use the worst peak.
- Full memory time series from before load through token 128.
- Record `mx.get_peak_memory()`, process resident memory, system memory pressure, and swap counters.

Pass rule:

```text
H = 128 GiB - worst_process_peak
PASS iff H >= 19.2 GiB
         and swapout delta = 0
         and no allocator/wired-limit warning
         and all three runs reach token 128
```

Also run the 1,024-token mechanism shape once per `dense`, `moe-k8`, and `moe-k4` to expose KV/trace-scale failures not exercised by the 128-token fit probe.

### D. Runtime and workload validity

Require:

- Three successful greedy smokes per arm.
- Identical prompt IDs and chat-template bytes across the dense/MoE pair.
- Runtime-observed output counts and stop reasons.
- `axi-sd-quality-screen-v1`: 256 answer-keyed items, 64 per stratum, with no LLM judge and no post-output exclusions, as frozen at [scorecard lines 296–318](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/specs/axi/sd_model_pair_scorecard.md:296).
- Dense/MoE quality-band pass: overall gap ≤0.05 and every stratum gap ≤0.10.
- Exact output identity, edit distance, output length, and stop distribution reported even when the quality band passes.

### E. Four-hour envelope timing probe

After one discarded warm-up, time at least three full `moe-routing-fixed1024-v1` members for each future arm: dense, k=8, and k=4. Include load/reload, request setup, decode, post-request trace flush, cooldown/admission, references, calibration brackets, and custody overhead.

Compute:

```text
T_plan =
  fixed calibration/reference overhead
  + Σ_arm n_arm × upper_p90(member_time_arm + cooldown_time_arm)
  + trace-flush/storage time
```

The candidate night is feasible only if `T_plan ≤ 192 minutes`, preserving 48 minutes as the required 20% margin inside four hours. Report schedules for:

- Two-night minimum: independently governed floor night plus science night.
- Three-night fallback: dense floor, k8/k4 floors, and science split prospectively.

No optimistic packing using mean member time. If neither schedule fits, kill the MoE nights.

### DG2 exit

All joined receipts pass; the quality screen passes or receives the pre-authorized trade-off disposition; memory passes worst-of-three; the frozen schedule fits within 192 minutes. Otherwise stop.

## DG3 — Observability week

### Source finding and required runtime posture

The referee’s `qwen3_next/qwen3_5` path applies to the retired Qwen3.5-122B candidate:

- `qwen3_5.py` imports `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` at [line 21](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_5.py:21) and defaults to normalized routing weights at [line 51](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_5.py:51).
- `qwen3_next.py` forms `inds` and `scores` at [lines 334–344](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_next.py:334), then adds the shared expert at line 346.

The selected Qwen3-30B artifact instead dispatches through:

- `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` at [line 110](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:110).
- Native `top_k` and normalization state at [lines 116–121](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:116).
- Router probabilities, expert IDs, routing weights, normalization, and dispatch at [lines 127–137](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:127).

`inds` and `scores` are local intermediates with no callback or observer seam. Therefore a fork—or equivalently a maintained patch overlay—is required. A monkey-patch that recomputes routing is not acceptable evidence.

### Minimal instrumentation design

Create a derived runtime from exact `mlx-lm 0.31.3` source:

- Add an optional `RoutingTraceSink` to `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock`.
- Capture the original `inds` and post-normalization `scores` immediately before `switch_mlp`; never recompute them.
- Attach immutable `layer_id`, request ID, phase, and token position.
- Add a config-only `routing_top_k_override`; native k=8 and forced k=4 share identical code.
- With tracing disabled, execute the original source path exactly.
- With tracing enabled, retain lazy on-device references during decode; perform no host readback, logging, serialization, or `mx.eval` solely for tracing inside the measured interval.
- Flush after `decode_end` and the telemetry stop marker.
- Hash-bind the sidecar to request, config, model, runtime, and bundle identities.

Minimum record:

```text
request_id, phase, token_position, layer_id,
configured_k, realized_k,
expert_ids[], normalized_router_weights[],
weight_sum, trace_sequence_number
```

All claim and floor arms use the instrumented derivative—even dense, where the routing sidecar is explicitly empty. Call the stack `mlx-lm 0.31.3+jwmoe1`, record the full source/package manifest, and do not inherit any stock-runtime floor.

### Realized-k reconciliation

For the Qwen3-30B decode trace:

- Expected records: `requests × realized decode tokens × 48 MoE layers`.
- k=8 records contain exactly eight distinct IDs; k=4 records contain exactly four.
- IDs are integers in `[0,127]`.
- Weights are finite, positive, correctly paired to IDs, and sum to 1 within a preregistered floating tolerance.
- No duplicate IDs, sequence gaps, overflow, dropped buffers, or missing final flush.
- Aggregate expert activations exactly equal `records × k`.
- Full expert-load counts reconcile with the per-record sidecar.
- `argpartition` ordering is not interpreted as rank ordering; ID/weight pairs and selected sets are preserved as emitted.
- The active-parameter ledger uses these realized dispatch sets. Configured k is diagnostic, never a substitute.

Any missing record makes the routing probe `FAIL(routing_probe_incomplete)` and removes the mechanism claim.

### ≤2% overhead protocol

For each k separately:

1. Freeze one full 128-prompt/1,024-output token stream.
2. Run 12 counterbalanced ABBA blocks after warm-up: trace disabled versus buffered trace enabled, same derived runtime, model resident.
3. Require exact output-token identity and identical stop reason within every pair.
4. Primary overhead is paired decode-duration change; report throughput and peak memory secondarily.
5. Compute the paired mean/median slowdown and a fixed 95% paired-bootstrap interval.
6. Pass only if the upper 95% bound is ≤2% for both k=8 and k=4.
7. Require zero trace loss and continued memory-headroom compliance.
8. Separately compare stock runtime with derived-runtime/no-op mode to demonstrate numerical identity; this is a capability check, not permission to transfer floors.

If the upper bound exceeds 2%, do not subtract overhead. Either remove routing-mechanism claims and study only the named stack contrast, or kill the MoE paper. The instrumented and stock runtimes remain distinct stack identities even if the point estimate is zero.

### DG3 exit

Instrumented package hash frozen; unit and live Metal smokes pass; 100% reconciliation; both overhead bounds ≤2%; trace flush is demonstrably outside the measured interval.

## DG4 — Estimand week

### Frozen comparison matrix

Use all 256 items from `axi-sd-quality-screen-v1`; do not select prompts based on observed divergence.

For each prompt:

1. Free-run native k=8 under `axi-sd-greedy-eos128-v1`, yielding sequence `S8`.
2. Free-run forced k=4, yielding `S4`.
3. Teacher-force `S8` through both k=8 and k=4.
4. Teacher-force `S4` through both k=8 and k=4.
5. Run the dense model on both fixed sequences as a descriptive content-control companion.

This gives a symmetric `routing budget × supplied sequence` design. It avoids privileging the native sequence and separates expert-budget effects from text-content effects.

Repeat the timing-only teacher-forced analysis at `k ∈ {2,4,6,8}` on the lexicographically selected 32-item subset already defined by the scorecard’s prospective subset rule. k=2 and k=6 are desk diagnostics only; the eventual energy contrast remains k=8 versus k=4.

### Required reports

For every free-running pair:

- First divergent token position.
- Exact-token identity rate and common-prefix length.
- Token edit distance.
- Output length and stop reason.
- Repetition-loop and invalid-output flags.
- Overall and per-stratum deterministic quality scores.

For every arm, layer, request, and before/after first divergence:

- Unique experts touched.
- Expert-load distribution and CV.
- Selected-weight entropy.
- Expert-set persistence/Jaccard overlap across adjacent tokens.
- Consecutive reuse rate and reuse distance.
- Router-load concentration/HHI.
- Realized k and trace completeness.

Primary comparisons:

- Fixed-content k8−k4 duration/throughput difference on `S8`.
- Same difference on `S4`.
- Sequence-content effect at fixed k.
- Budget-by-sequence interaction.
- Free-running k8−k4 result reported separately as a deployment effect.

Use prompt as the inference unit. Tokens, layers, and experts are nested observations, not independent replicates.

### DG4 dispositions

- `PASS-QE`: k4 meets the same overall/per-stratum quality band against k8, traces reconcile, and the fixed-content effect is estimable.
- `PASS-TRADEOFF`: k4 falls outside the quality band but remains executable/nondegenerate, and Ed prospectively authorized a trade-off paper.
- `FAIL`: catastrophic looping/invalid output, forced replay unsupported, routing evidence incomplete, or content and budget effects cannot be separated.

Free-running divergence never invalidates the teacher-forced estimand, but it forbids describing the free-running energy difference as “the cost of four experts.”

## Sublinearity-thesis preregistration

### Model

For prompt `p` and routing budget `k`, define:

```text
B_proxy(p,k) = B_fixed + B_routed(p,k)
t(p,k)       = alpha + beta × B_proxy(p,k)
               + gamma × expert_churn(p,k) + prompt_effect
E(p,k)       = mean_decode_power(p,k) × t(p,k)
```

`B_proxy` is a tensor-byte demand proxy computed from the exact quantized tensor inventory and realized expert IDs. It is not claimed to be measured DRAM traffic. `B_fixed` includes embeddings/head, attention, norms, router, and other always-executed tensors. Qwen3-30B has no Qwen3.5-style shared-expert term unless the runtime tensor ledger proves otherwise.

Define the byte-proportional expected fractional saving:

```text
s_bytes = [B_proxy(k=8) - B_proxy(k=4)] / B_proxy(k=8)
```

and observed energy saving:

```text
s_energy = [E(k=8) - E(k=4)] / E(k=8)
rho      = s_energy / s_bytes
```

### Frozen predictions

1. `E8 > E4` and `t8 > t4`.
2. Savings are sublinear relative to the byte-demand model: `rho < 1`.
3. Confirmatory sublinearity requires the upper 95% confidence bound for `rho` to be below 1 and the energy direction to clear its operative floor. Otherwise report `sublinearity_not_resolved`.
4. Teacher-forced k={2,4,6,8} timing will show a positive fixed intercept; halving routed bytes will reduce duration by less than half.
5. Greater expert churn/lower reuse will predict worse effective byte throughput at fixed k; this is a routing-locality association, not per-expert causal energy attribution.
6. The dense stack is predicted to achieve higher proxy-byte throughput than MoE k=8, but this cross-model comparison remains descriptive because architecture and tensor layout differ.
7. No exact “40% bandwidth efficiency” claim is preregistered without a hardware traffic counter. The paper may say “consistent with dispatch/locality overhead” when only byte proxies and timing are observed.

The preregistration freezes equations, tensor-byte accounting, endpoints, intervals, multiplicity, and forbidden upgrades before Gate 5 sees any energy result.

The referee’s `qwen3_next/qwen3_5` path applies to the retired Qwen3.5-122B candidate:

- `qwen3_5.py` imports `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` at [line 21](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_5.py:21) and defaults to normalized routing weights at [line 51](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_5.py:51).
- `qwen3_next.py` forms `inds` and `scores` at [lines 334–344](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_next.py:334), then adds the shared expert at line 346.

The selected Qwen3-30B artifact instead dispatches through:

- `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` at [line 110](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:110).
- Native `top_k` and normalization state at [lines 116–121](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:116).
- Router probabilities, expert IDs, routing weights, normalization, and dispatch at [lines 127–137](/Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm/models/qwen3_moe.py:127).

`inds` and `scores` are local intermediates with no callback or observer seam. Therefore a fork—or equivalently a maintained patch overlay—is required. A monkey-patch that recomputes routing is not acceptable evidence.

### Minimal instrumentation design

Create a derived runtime from exact `mlx-lm 0.31.3` source:

- Add an optional `RoutingTraceSink` to `Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock`.
- Capture the original `inds` and post-normalization `scores` immediately before `switch_mlp`; never recompute them.
- Attach immutable `layer_id`, request ID, phase, and token position.
- Add a config-only `routing_top_k_override`; native k=8 and forced k=4 share identical code.
- With tracing disabled, execute the original source path exactly.
- With tracing enabled, retain lazy on-device references during decode; perform no host readback, logging, serialization, or `mx.eval` solely for tracing inside the measured interval.
- Flush after `decode_end` and the telemetry stop marker.
- Hash-bind the sidecar to request, config, model, runtime, and bundle identities.

Minimum record:

```text
request_id, phase, token_position, layer_id,
configured_k, realized_k,
expert_ids[], normalized_router_weights[],
weight_sum, trace_sequence_number
```

All claim and floor arms use the instrumented derivative—even dense, where the routing sidecar is explicitly empty. Call the stack `mlx-lm 0.31.3+jwmoe1`, record the full source/package manifest, and do not inherit any stock-runtime floor.

### Realized-k reconciliation

For the Qwen3-30B decode trace:

- Expected records: `requests × realized decode tokens × 48 MoE layers`.
- k=8 records contain exactly eight distinct IDs; k=4 records contain exactly four.
- IDs are integers in `[0,127]`.
- Weights are finite, positive, correctly paired to IDs, and sum to 1 within a preregistered floating tolerance.
- No duplicate IDs, sequence gaps, overflow, dropped buffers, or missing final flush.
- Aggregate expert activations exactly equal `records × k`.
- Full expert-load counts reconcile with the per-record sidecar.
- `argpartition` ordering is not interpreted as rank ordering; ID/weight pairs and selected sets are preserved as emitted.
- The active-parameter ledger uses these realized dispatch sets. Configured k is diagnostic, never a substitute.

Any missing record makes the routing probe `FAIL(routing_probe_incomplete)` and removes the mechanism claim.

### ≤2% overhead protocol

For each k separately:

1. Freeze one full 128-prompt/1,024-output token stream.
2. Run 12 counterbalanced ABBA blocks after warm-up: trace disabled versus buffered trace enabled, same derived runtime, model resident.
3. Require exact output-token identity and identical stop reason within every pair.
4. Primary overhead is paired decode-duration change; report throughput and peak memory secondarily.
5. Compute the paired mean/median slowdown and a fixed 95% paired-bootstrap interval.
6. Pass only if the upper 95% bound is ≤2% for both k=8 and k=4.
7. Require zero trace loss and continued memory-headroom compliance.
8. Separately compare stock runtime with derived-runtime/no-op mode to demonstrate numerical identity; this is a capability check, not permission to transfer floors.

If the upper bound exceeds 2%, do not subtract overhead. Either remove routing-mechanism claims and study only the named stack contrast, or kill the MoE paper. The instrumented and stock runtimes remain distinct stack identities even if the point estimate is zero.

### DG3 exit

Instrumented package hash frozen; unit and live Metal smokes pass; 100% reconciliation; both overhead bounds ≤2%; trace flush is demonstrably outside the measured interval.

## DG4 — Estimand week

### Frozen comparison matrix

Use all 256 items from `axi-sd-quality-screen-v1`; do not select prompts based on observed divergence.

For each prompt:

1. Free-run native k=8 under `axi-sd-greedy-eos128-v1`, yielding sequence `S8`.
2. Free-run forced k=4, yielding `S4`.
3. Teacher-force `S8` through both k=8 and k=4.
4. Teacher-force `S4` through both k=8 and k=4.

This gives a symmetric `routing budget × supplied sequence` design. It avoids privileging the native sequence and separates expert-budget effects from text-content effects.

Repeat the timing-only teacher-forced analysis at `k ∈ {2,4,6,8}` on the lexicographically selected 32-item subset already defined by the scorecard’s prospective subset rule. k=2 and k=6 are desk diagnostics only; the eventual energy contrast remains k=8 versus k=4.

### Required reports

For every free-running pair:

- First divergent token position.
- Exact-token identity rate and common-prefix length.
- Token edit distance.
- Output length and stop reason.
- Repetition-loop and invalid-output flags.
- Overall and per-stratum deterministic quality scores.

For every arm, layer, request, and before/after first divergence:

- Unique experts touched.
- Expert-load distribution and CV.
- Selected-weight entropy.
- Expert-set persistence/Jaccard overlap across adjacent tokens.
- Consecutive reuse rate and reuse distance.
- Router-load concentration/HHI.
- Realized k and trace completeness.

Primary comparisons:

- Fixed-content k8−k4 duration/throughput difference on `S8`.
- Same difference on `S4`.
- Sequence-content effect at fixed k.
- Budget-by-sequence interaction.
- Free-running k8−k4 result reported separately as a deployment effect.

Use prompt as the inference unit. Tokens, layers, and experts are nested observations, not independent replicates.

### DG4 dispositions

- `PASS-QE`: k4 meets the same overall/per-stratum quality band against k8, traces reconcile, and the fixed-content effect is estimable.
- `PASS-TRADEOFF`: k4 falls outside the quality band but remains executable/nondegenerate, and Ed prospectively authorized a trade-off paper.
- `FAIL`: catastrophic looping/invalid output, forced replay unsupported, routing evidence incomplete, or content and budget effects cannot be separated.

Free-running divergence never invalidates the teacher-forced estimand, but it forbids describing the free-running energy difference as “the cost of four experts.”

## Sublinearity-thesis preregistration

### Model

For prompt `p` and routing budget `k`, define:

```text
B_proxy(p,k) = B_fixed + B_routed(p,k)
t(p,k)       = alpha + beta × B_proxy(p,k)
               + gamma × expert_churn(p,k) + prompt_effect
E(p,k)       = mean_decode_power(p,k) × t(p,k)
```

`B_proxy` is a tensor-byte demand proxy computed from the exact quantized tensor inventory and realized expert IDs. It is not claimed to be measured DRAM traffic. `B_fixed` includes embeddings/head, attention, norms, router, and other always-executed tensors. Qwen3-30B has no Qwen3.5-style shared-expert term unless the runtime tensor ledger proves otherwise.

Define the byte-proportional expected fractional saving:

```text
s_bytes = [B_proxy(k=8) - B_proxy(k=4)] / B_proxy(k=8)
```

and observed energy saving:

```text
s_energy = [E(k=8) - E(k=4)] / E(k=8)
rho      = s_energy / s_bytes
```

### Frozen predictions

1. `E8 > E4` and `t8 > t4`.
2. Savings are sublinear relative to the byte-demand model: `rho < 1`.
3. Confirmatory sublinearity requires the upper 95% confidence bound for `rho` to be below 1 and the energy direction to clear its operative floor. Otherwise report `sublinearity_not_resolved`.
4. Teacher-forced k={2,4,6,8} timing will show a positive fixed intercept; halving routed bytes will reduce duration by less than half.
5. Greater expert churn/lower reuse will predict worse effective byte throughput at fixed k; this is a routing-locality association, not per-expert causal energy attribution.
6. The dense stack is predicted to achieve higher proxy-byte throughput than MoE k=8, but this cross-model comparison remains descriptive because architecture and tensor layout differ.
7. No exact “40% bandwidth efficiency” claim is preregistered without a hardware traffic counter. The paper may say “consistent with dispatch/locality overhead” when only byte proxies and timing are observed.

The preregistration freezes equations, tensor-byte accounting, endpoints, intervals, multiplicity, and forbidden upgrades before Gate 5 sees any energy result.
